extracted.intended_audience: bibliometric researchers, research librarians, information scientists, and research managers interested in journal citation analysis
extracted.subtask_description: Describing and evaluating methods for identifying core journals and research fronts, mapping co-citation relationships, and measuring the size, composition, temporal history, and national distribution of citation-based research fronts in physical chemistry and chemical physics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection of core journals (SCI-indexed core set)
rubrics_metrics.description: The study focuses on 31 periodicals (core physical chemistry/chemical physics journals) indexed by the SCI in 1983 (listed in Table 1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define a core journal set explicitly (here: the 31 SCI-indexed titles) as the basis for subsequent citation and research-front analyses; present the list (Table 1) so that counts and representations can be computed relative to this core.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research-front definition
rubrics_metrics.description: A research front consists of a group of current papers that cites one or more older well-cited papers. It also includes the core papers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify fronts by grouping current publications that co-cite older, highly cited ('core') documents; the presence of such older well-cited papers defines and anchors the front.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identifying current concerns via research-front data
rubrics_metrics.description: The latter (current concerns) were identified by examining LSI's 1983 research-front data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use research-front outputs from citation databases (LSI/SCI research-front data) to identify topical 'current concerns' in the fields under study rather than relying solely on ad hoc topic lists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Total number of citing documents per front (size of a front)
rubrics_metrics.description: Counts of papers published in a research front (e.g., 'about 1,100 papers were published' for a given front).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the absolute count of citing publications in a front as a basic measure of its size and activity; report the total number of papers associated with each front to gauge prominence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number of citations to core (older well-cited) documents
rubrics_metrics.description: The number of citations from front papers to the older core documents (e.g., 'they cited 95 core documents' in the example front).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure how many distinct core documents are being cited by the front and the total citations to those core documents to characterize the intellectual anchors and cohesion of the front.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representation of front papers in core vs non-core journals
rubrics_metrics.description: Quantify how many front papers appear in the core journal set versus in non-core journals (e.g., 'only about 260 of the papers were published in 13 of the core journals; over 800 papers were published in non-core journals').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report proportions and counts of front publications appearing in the predefined core journals as an indicator of where the front is concentrated and how much of its activity lies outside the core.

rubrics_metrics.name: Table metrics: column-level reporting (columns C and D)
rubrics_metrics.description: Column C of Table 2 provides the number of 1983 articles from these core journals; Column D lists the number of core journal articles that cite the research front.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When tabulating fronts, include explicit per-front columns such as (C) number of articles from core journals in the front and (D) number of core-journal articles that cite the front so readers can assess journal-level engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Temporal citation history (citation trajectory)
rubrics_metrics.description: Plotting a paper's citation history over time (example: 'Figure 1 is a graph of this paper’s citation history from 1955 to 1984' for J.W. Gibbs’s paper) to reveal delayed recognition or changes in influence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use longitudinal citation plots to reveal patterns such as delayed recognition, growth, or decline of influence; interpret peaks, trends, and co-citation accrual over defined time windows.

rubrics_metrics.name: Co-citation mapping conventions (nodes, links, distances)
rubrics_metrics.description: Nodes represent co-citation strength, and distance is an indicator of semantic distance; serial numbers are for identification only; lines between nodes indicate relationships.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In co-citation maps, use node size/labels to reflect co-citation strength, spatial distance to represent semantic relatedness, and labeled serial numbers only as identifiers; explain map conventions so readers correctly interpret strength vs semantic proximity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of semantic/co-citation maps to reveal field interrelationships
rubrics_metrics.description: Maps showing semantic connections make it easier to view the complex interactions between chemistry and physics (e.g., Figure 2 and Figure 4 show molecular-orbital fronts and the borderland between chemistry and physics).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Produce and interpret maps of co-citation/semantic relationships to identify interdisciplinary linkages, boundary nodes (e.g., biochemistry point #38), and how subfields cluster or overlap.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection/prioritization of fronts for focused analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify and concentrate on the fronts that are most prominently seen in the core journals (the list of fronts most prominently seen in these journals is given in Table 2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize fronts for in-depth study by their prominence within the core journal set (e.g., representation counts, citation counts) rather than by absolute novelty alone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Country-by-country contribution metric
rubrics_metrics.description: Table 3 shows the percentage by country of citing papers to a research front (e.g., percent of citing papers from Japan, US, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use country-affiliation data of citing papers to produce national profiles of contribution to a front; report both absolute counts and percentages for international comparison.

rubrics_metrics.name: Using mapped research-front topics to interpret topical breadth and journal distribution
rubrics_metrics.description: The research-front topic lists and maps (e.g., molecular-orbital studies, kinetics on metal catalysts, Fischer-Tropsch synthesis, etc.) illustrate topical breadth and distribution across journals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List representative topic labels for fronts and show how specific methodological or topical clusters map to journals and subfields to help readers see subject-matter coverage and disciplinary spread.
